Five panes compile one file: three DXC and two Clang. Only the preprocessor
define differs between the repro and control arms.

Panes 1 and 3 are the declaration exactly as filed, on current DXC and on a 2021
release. Look at the exit status rather than the text: DXC terminates abnormally
instead of emitting a diagnostic, and on Compiler Explorer's Linux process a
Windows status is truncated to its low byte, so the number will not match what a
Windows build prints. Pane 2 adds -DCONTROL, which swaps in the supported
spelling of the same 16-bit type and changes nothing else; it compiles and emits
a shader, which is what shows the failure is about the declaration and not about
the profile, the flags or the entry point.

Panes 4 and 5 are the successor front end on the same two arms, syntax-only. It
rejects the repro arm with a parse diagnostic and accepts the control arm, so the
diagnostic is specific to this declaration rather than to the shader stage.

Compiler Explorer runs Release builds, so no assert is visible here. A local
assert-enabled build stops earlier, in the parser, on a null type; continuing
past that assert reaches the same memory fault the Release panes show.
